answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying identity to costly, verifiable work history rather than free sign-ups: each agent builds a reputation haven only after many completed, peer-reviewed jobs, and that standing decays if it goes idle. New identities start in a low-trust dune of tiny tasks, earning larger work only through consistent delivery, while a ferrous bond — a small refundable stake slashed for fraud — makes spawning thousands of fake agents expensive and unprofitable.
